newsitem.title: DUBAI: Archaeologists unearth ancient relics in Iran-paper.
newsitem.headline: Archaeologists unearth ancient relics in Iran-paper.

text.p: Archaeologists in Iran have unearthed ancient relics including human remains and a copper object dating back up to 8,000 years, the daily Tehran Times newspaper said on Thursday.
Amir Sarrafi, head of the excavation team, said excavations at a site in Rey near Tehran had revealed relics from 3500 BC, 5500 BC and 6000 BC, the English-language paper said.
"An interesting discovery made by the excavation team...is a tomb containing skeletal remains of a man," the paper said. It did not indicate the age of the remains.

"Excavations have also led to findings that the dead during that time were buried much like an embryo in a mother's womb, with the legs folded into the abdomen, perhaps to give a man's departure from this world the same appearance as that when he/she comes into this world," the paper quoted Sarrafi as saying.

Sarrafi said the most important discovery was a copper object inside a jar. He said the find indicated that residents of the region in the sixth millennium BC had already developed the technology of melting and creating copper objects.
